summary: Free tutorial that teaches how large language models work from scratch, including building and training your own small LLaMA-style model.

heroCommands.command: Read online, or clone the repo: git clone https://github.com/datawhalechina/happy-llm.git

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Happy-LLM is a systematic LLM learning tutorial from Datawhale. It starts with NLP basics and works through Transformers, pre-trained models and large models, then has you implement a complete LLaMA2-style model and train it from pre-training to fine-tuning.
sixtySeconds.problem: Many people use LLMs without understanding how they work. Happy-LLM explains the core principles and has you build one yourself.
whoFor: Developers wanting to train a small model
Readers who know Python and some ML
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a free, structured book-style course with hands-on code, covering everything up to RAG, agents and agentic RL.
requirements: Python and basic machine learning knowledge
A GPU helps for the training chapters

overview: Chapters cover NLP concepts, the Transformer architecture, pre-trained language models, large language models, building a large model from scratch (LLaMA2, tokenizer, small LLM pre-training), training practice (pre-training, SFT, LoRA/QLoRA), applications (evaluation, RAG, agents) and agentic RL (GRPO, Search-R1, ReTool).
Read it online or in the repo's docs folder; the chapter files are written in Chinese, with an English README. There is also an extra chapter of community blog posts.
All content is free. It is licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so non-commercial use with attribution.
